newsitem.title: USA: BHP Copper labor talks set for arbitration -union.
newsitem.headline: BHP Copper labor talks set for arbitration -union.

text.p: Labor talks at BHP Copper's U.S. operations have failed to reach agreement over pay and it appeared inevitable that arbitration would be invoked, Robert Guadiana, lead negotiator for the United Steelworkers of America said.
BHP took over the former Magma Copper operations in San Manuel and Pinto Valley in Arizona.
"We have not been able to reach agreement on money and benefits, and subsequently we are going to have to go to arbitration," Guadiana said. "This is brand new for us in copper."
Workers at the plants signed a 15-year framework deal June 1991 with provision for review every five years.
There was still some time left before the June 30 deadline to reach agreement before arbitration, but this appeared unlikely at the present time, Guadiana said.
The arbitration panel could take up to next January to reach an outcome which would be binding on both sides for a year, he added.

"We don't have the right to strike, and the company does not have the right to lock us out," Guadiana said. "But this could have a very negative impact on attitude of people and could really impact productivity."

Meanwhile Guadiana said there was still no meetings scheduled in the stalled labor talks at Phelps Dodge Corp's Chino copper mine in New Mexico where workers have been without contract since June 30 last year.
